name: Map priority food-production areas (including taro patches, household gardens, community or designated food islands, nurseries and other locally important production area) using community knowledge and available technical data.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.2.1 "Document community owned resources", $10,235 (2015) x population Chuuk / Yap = $61,361 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. No Chuuk JSAP 2016 or IDP equivalent. Community resource documentation, scaled by population.

name: Assess current and future exposure of priority agricultural areas to saltwater intrusion, coastal flooding, extreme rainfall, drought, heat and erosion.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.1.1 "Assessment of vulnerabilities and opportunities (mangrove planting)", $153,620 (2016) = $212,657 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Analogue: statewide sector vulnerability assessment of similar scope. The same line also costs 4.2.1.

name: Undertake agricultural suitability studies and farmer-led trials to identify locally acceptable crops and production systems for locations where current crops are becoming less reliable.
justification: Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.1 "Feasibility study on needs and appropriateness of salt and drought resistant crops", $32,284 (2016) = $44,691 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. State-level study, no scaling.

name: Record key access and land-use constraints that affect food-system resilience, including customary access to shared food areas, without attempting to formalise or alter customary ownership.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.2.1 "Document community owned resources", $10,235 (2015) = $14,347 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. State-level record linked to 3.1.1 mapping, no scaling.

name: Create a simple State food-security and adaptation register that links identified risks, existing projects, trial results, priority sites and proposed investments.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.5.1 "Establish and maintain database on salt and drought tolerant crops", $5,692 (2015) = $7,979 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. One State register, no scaling.

name: Develop practical seasonal and climate information products for farmers and fishers, linked where possible to existing weather, drought and early-warning systems.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.3 "Develop specific communication and awareness raising strategy", $4,569 (2016) = $6,325 (2026). Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.3 "Prepare and broadcast radio talkback", $10,554 (2016) = $14,610 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Analogue from shoreline awareness.

name: Establish simple monitoring of salinity, flooding, crop condition, planting success and post-event recovery in priority taro and food-production areas.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 4.3.1 "Setting up weather stations in selected islands", $86,695 (2016) = $120,012 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Analogue: monitoring equipment network in selected islands.

name: Review food-system impacts after major events and use findings to update crop trials, recovery stocks, drainage priorities and project design.
justification: No separate cost. Included in 1.7.1 and 1.7.6 (post-event reviews cover agriculture). Removed to avoid double counting with 1.7.1.

name: Develop community nurseries and decentralised planting-material banks for locally important crops, including vegetatively propagated crops where conventional seed banks are not suitable.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.4.4 "Provide planting materials (salt resilient taro) to all islands", $342,600 (2016) = $474,262 (2026). Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.1 "Set up nurseries for raising crops on main and outer islands", $59,970 (2016) x population Chuuk / Pohnpei = $111,590 (2026). Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.1 "Maintenance of nurseries", $11,400 (2016) x population Chuuk / Pohnpei = $21,213 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match for planting material supply. Nursery set-up not costed in Chuuk JSAP 2016; scaled by population.

name: Protect and document locally adapted crop varieties and traditional planting materials, including knowledge on propagation, storage, replanting and recovery after saltwater or storm damage.
justification: Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.6 "Document practices on food preservation", $37,808 (2016) = $52,338 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Analogue for documenting traditional varieties and knowledge.

name: Design resilient storage arrangements for tools, seeds and planting material, including protection from heat, moisture, pests, flooding and storm damage.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.5.1 "Establish seed banks on Yap proper and neighbouring islands", $14,485 (2015) x population Chuuk / Yap = $86,841 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Prepare rapid agriculture damage and recovery protocols linking DEOC, agriculture staff, municipalities and community focal points, including clear triggers for releasing and replacing stocks.
justification: No separate cost. Included in 1.1.5 (roles and protocols between DEOC and sector agencies). Removed to avoid using Chuuk JSAP 2016 line 1.6.1 twice.

name: Assess whether livestock breeding or broodstock continuity measures are relevant for Chuuk communities and include them only where local production systems justify them.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.5.3 "Assessment including species feasibility study", $12,500 (2015) = $17,522 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Assessment only. If justified, Yap 3.5.6 livestock gene pool ($39,900, 2015) gives an implementation reference.

name: Pre-plan inter-island transport and storage arrangements for recovery materials so priority outer islands can be reached quickly after events.
justification: No separate cost. Included in 1.4.1 and 1.4.2 (emergency logistics and pre-positioning).

name: Pilot salt-tolerant, flood-tolerant, heat-tolerant or otherwise climate-resilient crop varieties through farmer-led demonstration plots in locations where existing crops are becoming less reliable.
justification: Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.1 "Distribute seedlings of salt resistant crops", $24,080 (2016) x population Chuuk / Pohnpei = $44,807 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Support locally appropriate crop diversification to spread climate and livelihood risk, using crops selected with farmers and communities rather than a fixed State-wide crop list.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.5.1 "Distribute seedlings of salt resistant crops", $16,155 (2015) x population Chuuk / Yap = $96,853 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Retain and refine elevated taro beds, raised gardens and other locally used techniques for low-lying or flood-prone sites where communities consider them effective.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.4.2 "Introduce gardening and elevate gardens on low islands", $351,000 (2016) = $485,891 (2026). Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.4.3 "Elevate taro beds and create artificial beds on atoll islands", $549,400 (2016) = $760,536 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Promote agroforestry and replanting of locally important perennial food and multipurpose species where site conditions and community priorities support them.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.4.5 "Encourage coconut and banana replanting", $318,800 (2016) = $441,316 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match for perennial replanting.

name: Improve soil health through mulching, compost or other locally feasible organic amendments, soil-cover practices and erosion control.
justification: IDP: Chuuk IDP 2025-2034 S17 "Chuuk Compost Facility (pending, SPREP)", $100,000 (2024) = $105,915 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Compost supply for organic soil amendments.

name: Strengthen integrated pest and disease management and improve early detection and response to invasive species that threaten croplands and planting stock.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.3.1 "Neighbouring islands invasive species survey", $28,000 (2015) x population Chuuk / Yap = $167,866 (2026). Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.3.1 "Engage community in invasive species management", $6,500 (2015) x population Chuuk / Yap = $38,969 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Assess suitable higher-ground areas for voluntary expansion or relocation of food production on high islands where low-lying production is increasingly exposed, accounting for soil, water, access and land tenure.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.4.1 "Move farms to higher grounds: soil tests in higher lands and advocacy", $267,425 (2016) = $370,197 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Map and assess drainage, waterlogging, drought and irrigation constraints in priority taro patches, gardens and agricultural areas.
justification: Not costed: No costed agricultural drainage assessment found. Earlier draft used a Pohnpei crop feasibility study as a unit-cost analogue; removed as low confidence.

name: Clear, repair and maintain existing agricultural drains, channels and small water-control structures before constructing new systems.
justification: Other source: Palau PACC food security BCA 2012 Table 7 "Improving the waterways, hired labour per taro patch site", $6,720 (2012) x regions x priority sites per region = $97,244 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Assumes 10 priority sites (2 per region).

name: Design and implement small-scale drainage improvements to reduce prolonged flooding and support recovery of food-production areas after extreme rainfall and coastal inundation.
justification: Other source: Palau PACC food security BCA 2012 p.40 "Public cost of dikes and flood and flow gates, 3-year roll-out (3 x $22,500)", $67,500 (2012) x number of Chuuk regions = $488,392 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. One roll-out per Chuuk region.

name: Pilot low-cost, water-efficient irrigation systems suited to household and community-scale agriculture, with simple maintenance requirements.
justification: Other source: Palau PACC food security BCA 2012 Tables 6-7 "Ngimis taro patch demonstration site, establishment and completion ($9,361 + $12,100)", $21,461 (2012) x number of Chuuk regions = $155,280 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. One pilot per Chuuk region.

name: Assess and deploy small farm rainwater systems or micro-reservoirs where they can provide a realistic drought buffer without competing with drinking-water needs.
justification: Not costed: No farm rainwater source found. Chuuk JSAP 2016 4.1.3 catchments now costs 2.2.3 (drinking water).

name: Use mulching, soil cover and other water-conservation practices to reduce irrigation demand and retain soil moisture.
justification: Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.1 "Training for vegetable gardens", $4,500 (2016) x population Chuuk / Pohnpei = $8,373 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Establish local operations and maintenance arrangements for shared drains, pumps, reservoirs or irrigation systems, including cleaning schedules, spare parts and responsibility for repairs.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.2.1 "Development of Community Management Plan", $5,692 (2015) x number of Chuuk regions = $39,894 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. One O&M arrangement per region.

name: Assess climate, ecosystem and harvesting pressures affecting priority coastal fisheries and aquaculture areas, using community observations and available marine data.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.2.1 "Community assessment of natural resource management needs and priorities", $52,935 (2015) = $74,203 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. State-level assessment, no scaling.

name: Assess hatchery, pond, mariculture or other sustainable aquaculture options identified in NDC 3.0, selecting species only after ecological, market, biosecurity and operations and maintenance feasibility is confirmed.
justification: Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.2 "Feasibility study on aquaculture and coastal fisheries", $26,900 (2016) = $37,238 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. State-level study, no scaling.

name: Document traditional aquaculture practices, including rock-pool fish farming where communities identify relevant knowledge, sites and interest in revival.
justification: Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.6 "Document practices on food preservation (unit-cost analogue)", $37,808 (2016) = $52,338 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Documentation study, no scaling.

name: Pilot revival or adaptation of traditional aquaculture practices where ecological, cultural and technical assessment shows they remain viable.
justification: Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.3 "Establish fish stock", $31,085 (2016) x population Chuuk / Pohnpei = $57,842 (2026). Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.3 "Distribute fish stock", $12,630 (2016) x population Chuuk / Pohnpei = $23,501 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Strengthen community-based fisheries management where declining resources are linked to fishing pressure, using locally appropriate rules such as closures, gear controls or other customary and statutory measures.
justification: Other source: MCT Adaptation Fund proposal 2017 Output 3.2 "Community eco-based adaptation grant, average per community project", $40,000 (2017) x number of Chuuk regions = $271,086 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. One community fisheries management grant per region.

name: Coordinate restoration and protection of mangroves, seagrass, reefs and other fish habitats with Package 4 (Coastal & Ecosystem Resilience).
justification: No separate cost. Coordination only. Habitat restoration is costed under 4.2 and 4.7.

name: Build local aquaculture skills in water quality, feeding, disease and biosecurity management, harvesting, business management and equipment maintenance.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.5.2 "Community training on agroforestry (training unit cost)", $12,692 (2015) x population Chuuk / Yap = $76,091 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Improve community and State monitoring of fisheries condition, catch trends and aquaculture performance so decisions can respond to both climate and harvesting pressures.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.1.1 "GIS train the trainer", $29,823 (2015) = $41,805 (2026). Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.1.2 "Assess training and equipment needs (GIS, GPS)", $12,923 (2015) = $18,115 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Monitoring and data capacity, no scaling. No scaling.

name: Assess post-harvest losses and climate/disaster vulnerabilities across local food supply chains, including harvest, storage, processing, power, water, transport and market access.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.4.6 "Conduct feasibility study (coconut processing plant)", $59,750 (2016) = $82,712 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Analogue for supply-chain loss assessment.

name: Identify priority household, community and commercial food-storage gaps, including needs for dry storage, resilient community stores and cold storage where a viable operating model exists.
justification: Not costed: No costed food-storage gap study found (earlier low-confidence analogue removed).

name: Support climate-resilient food preservation and processing practices, including locally appropriate traditional methods that reduce spoilage and improve emergency food availability.
justification: Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.5 "Procure, distribute and monitor taro and breadfruit mills", $168,560 (2016) x population Chuuk / Pohnpei = $313,649 (2026). Other source: Pohnpei JSAP 2016 4.1.6 "Training in schools and communities, food packaging, promotional materials ($17,277 + $20,015 + $14,308)", $51,600 (2016) x population Chuuk / Pohnpei = $96,015 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Upgrade or develop storage and processing facilities with appropriate drainage, structural resilience, water, sanitation, ventilation, backup power and maintenance arrangements.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.4.6 "Implement recommendations (revitalised coconut processing plant)", $2,015,050 (2016) = $2,789,441 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Cross-check: IDP AF1 + AF2 + MA3 = $2.55m (2024).

name: Develop contingency arrangements for food distribution to outer islands during transport disruption, linked to disaster risk management logistics and inter-island transport planning.
justification: Not costed: No costed food distribution contingency plan found (earlier low-confidence analogue removed).

name: Strengthen market information and producer-to-buyer linkages so farmers and fishers can sell diversified or climate-resilient products and reduce avoidable losses.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.5.5 "Identify potential markets; establish export support facility ($3,000 + $25,330)", $28,330 (2015) = $39,712 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. No scaling.

name: Support producer groups, cooperatives and private-sector partnerships for local processing and value addition where there is a realistic market and resilience benefit.
justification: Not costed: No costed producer-group support found. Cross-check: GCF SAP020 Component 3 ($1.06m FSM-wide) includes market linkages.

name: Strengthen routine agriculture extension and outer-island outreach for climate-resilient farming, soil management, pest management, crop recovery and farm water practices.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.5.2 "Community training on agroforestry, aimed at youth", $12,692 (2015) x population Chuuk / Yap = $76,091 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Strengthen fisheries and aquaculture extension for community-based management, aquaculture operations, biosecurity, water quality, handling and livelihood development.
justification: Not costed: No costed fisheries extension programme found (earlier agroforestry training analogue removed).

name: Document and support intergenerational transfer of traditional knowledge relevant to crop diversity, taro recovery, food preservation, fishing and aquaculture, subject to community consent.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.5.4 "Document traditional food preservation practices; training and promotion ($58,208 + $41,985)", $100,192 (2015) = $140,446 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. No scaling.

name: Provide practical financial literacy, business planning and climate-finance readiness for producer groups where commercial or cooperative activities are being developed.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 3.4.1 "Participation in climate finance talks; grant writing trainings", $21,355 (2016) = $29,562 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Develop farmer and fisher climate-information support in accessible formats and local language where feasible, linked to Activity 3.1 and existing warning/forecast systems.
justification: No separate cost. Included in 3.1.6 (climate information products).

name: Create a simple learning and feedback process so extension staff record which adaptation measures are being adopted, where support is failing and what communities need next.
justification: Not costed: No costed extension feedback system found (earlier analogue removed).

name: Undertake a cross-island coastal risk and adaptation assessment (covering settlements, taro and food-production areas, roads, docks, public facilities, water sources, cultural sites and important ecosystems).
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.2 "Carry out vulnerability assessment", $372,032 (2016) = $515,005 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Carry out site-specific wave, erosion, inundation, sediment and shoreline-change assessments at priority locations before selecting structural or ecosystem measures.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.2.4 "Modelling to identify appropriate coastal defence systems", $88,269 (2015) = $123,733 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Chuuk JSAP 2016 has no site-level coastal modelling line.

name: Map existing shoreline structures and nature-based projects, recording condition, function, ownership, maintenance arrangements and known failure or damage history.
justification: Not costed: No costed shoreline structure inventory found. Chuuk JSAP 2016 4.3.1 spatial maps now costs 1.1.3.

name: Document community and traditional knowledge on historic shoreline positions, wave exposure, protected areas, culturally important sites and past local protection practices, with consent over sensitive information.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.5 "Improve communication tools; traditional knowledge mapping (before and after)", $15,419 (2016) = $21,345 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Establish simple shoreline benchmarks, fixed photo points and community observation sites, with repeat checks after major king tides and storms.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.7 "Annual inspection and assessment of coastal benchmarks", $740,463 (2016) = $1,025,026 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Prepare or update a Chuuk coastal management strategy linking shoreline protection, ecosystem restoration, land use, infrastructure planning and long-term settlement choices.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.1 "Coastal management plan: information collection, draft and endorse", $11,988 (2016) = $16,595 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Low for a strategy. Cross-check: Kosrae JSAP 2015 Objective 3.4 shoreline management $169,907.

name: Prepare site-specific coastal adaptation plans for the highest-risk locations, using transparent options analysis to compare no-build / maintenance, ecosystem restoration, hybrid works, seawalls, bunds, nourishment and longer-term transition options.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.2 "Prioritise areas for action; identify context-specific responses ($27,139 + $15,419)", $42,558 (2016) = $58,913 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match for options analysis.

name: Assess the condition, protective function and restoration suitability of existing mangrove and coastal vegetation areas (including land tenure, sediment conditions and likely future sea-level response).
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.1.1 "Mangrove assessment of vulnerabilities and opportunities; prioritise areas", $176,180 (2016) = $243,887 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Protect intact mangrove and coastal vegetation areas that already provide shoreline buffering, including community stewardship and controls on damaging clearance where appropriate.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.1.2 "Community awareness on mangrove planting (produce and disseminate materials)", $65,850 (2016) = $91,156 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Restore degraded mangrove or coastal vegetation at sites confirmed as ecologically and socially suitable.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.1.3 "Mangrove planting programme (nursery, seedlings, schools), stated sub-total", $71,500 (2016) = $98,978 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Line items sum to $111,400; the stated sub-total is used because it ties to the 2.1 total of $344,130.

name: Develop site stewardship agreements that clarify landowner consent, community roles, access, protection rules and who is responsible for maintenance and replanting.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.2.1 "Development of Community Management Plan", $5,692 (2015) x number of Chuuk regions = $39,894 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. One stewardship agreement process per region.

name: Provide practical training on site selection, planting, protection, maintenance and monitoring, using local ecological knowledge and technical guidance together.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.2.1 "Education and training on sustainable natural resource use, incorporating traditional knowledge", $6,850 (2015) x population Chuuk / Yap = $41,067 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Scaled by population.

name: Review or strengthen rules and awareness concerning removal or conversion of mangroves and other important natural coastal buffers.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 2.1.4 "Mangrove protection legislation: draft and endorse", $30,600 (2016) = $42,360 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Identify high-risk sites where physical shoreline protection is justified after comparison with ecosystem, land-use and no-build / maintenance options.
justification: No separate cost. Included in 4.1.7 (site-specific options analysis).

name: Complete site-specific feasibility, coastal-process assessment, engineering design, alternatives analysis and environmental / social safeguards before construction.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.2.3 "Prepare climate-proof designs", $36,416 (2016) = $50,411 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Analogue. Design line only; the JSAP risk assessment line in the same objective now costs 5.1.2. IDP shoreline projects (CE1, CE3, AF3) are assumed to include their own design costs.

name: Assess and pilot bunds or stop banks where lower-cost protection is technically suitable, recognising their lower workshop ranking and site-specific role.
justification: Other source: Palau PACC food security BCA 2012 p.40, annex 1 "Earthen dike, 30 m section, average of three access levels ($9,600, $6,600, $6,300)", $7,500 (2012) x number of Chuuk regions = $54,266 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. One 30 m pilot per region.

name: Assess beach nourishment, wave attenuation, drainage improvements or other locally suitable shoreline measures as part of site-specific options analysis.
justification: No separate cost. Included in 4.1.2 and 4.1.7 (site assessment and options analysis).

name: Pilot hybrid protection that combines engineered elements with mangroves, vegetation, sediment management or other natural buffers where site conditions support them.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.4 "Community-based shoreline protection and beach nourishment (soft and hard), with traditional skills transfer", $1,740,317 (2016) = $2,409,127 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Repair or complete failed, damaged or unfinished shoreline structures where assessment confirms that the original protection function remains appropriate.
justification: IDP: Chuuk IDP 2025-2034 CE1 "Weno Climate Resilient Shoreline (rehabilitate)", $1,490,000 (2024) = $1,578,128 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match for repair or completion.

name: Construct or upgrade engineered seawalls / revetments only at high-risk sites where design confirms they are the preferred response.
justification: IDP: Chuuk IDP 2025-2034 CE3 "Weno Shoreline Protection (new)", $2,000,000 (2024) = $2,118,293 (2026). IDP: Chuuk IDP 2025-2034 AF3 "Uman Seawall and Pad", $10,000,000 (2024) = $10,591,463 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match. CE5 and CE6 lagoon docks and seawalls ($35m) are excluded because they are costed under 5.3.

name: Monitor adjacent shoreline response and environmental effects so structures can be repaired, redesigned or supplemented if they transfer erosion or do not perform as intended.
justification: No separate cost. Included in 4.1.5 (shoreline benchmarks and repeat monitoring).

name: Review existing State and municipal land-use, shoreline, building and environmental rules to identify where climate and coastal risk requirements are missing or unclear.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 6.1.1 "Public consultations on existing codes; develop standards and regulations ($19,852 + $19,792)", $39,644 (2015) = $55,572 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Analogue for rules review.

name: Use hazard maps and long-term climate information to identify areas where new critical facilities, major infrastructure or settlement expansion should be avoided or subject to additional conditions.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.2.1 "Zoning laws: community awareness, draft and endorse", $217,290 (2016) = $300,795 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Establish or strengthen rules controlling unsustainable removal of sand, gravel and coral aggregate from beaches and nearshore areas where extraction worsens erosion or damages natural coastal defence.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.1.6 "Shoreline protection regulations: draft laws and consultation with resource owners", $248,032 (2016) = $343,352 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Establish monitoring, community reporting and proportionate enforcement for damaging sediment extraction and shoreline disturbance.
justification: Other source: Kosrae JSAP 2015 3.4 "Shoreline management capacity, including monitoring and enforcement (objective total)", $169,907 (2015) = $238,170 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. State-level, no scaling.

name: Develop a clear environmental and social review checklist for shoreline projects, covering alternatives, ecosystem effects, fisheries, public access, cultural sites, land tenure and downstream / neighbouring impacts.
justification: Other source: Yap JSAP 2015 3.2.2 "Awareness and enforcement training for EPA staff", $23,092 (2015) = $32,370 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. No scaling.

name: Identify communities and critical assets where repeated flooding, erosion or saltwater intrusion may eventually exceed the practical limits of in-place protection or maintenance.
justification: Past JSAP: Chuuk JSAP 2016 1.7.1 "Assess risks to outer island communities", $379,240 (2016) = $524,983 (2026). Escalated to 2026 USD with US CPI-U. Direct match.

name: Assess the infrastructure and service requirements of potential higher-ground areas, including roads, water, sanitation, power, schools, health access, communications and safe transport.

name: Develop social, cultural, land-tenure, consent, compensation and grievance safeguards for any future planned relocation or higher-ground development process.
